##### Bipartite Random Network FFRCISTG

A bipartite graph is one where nodes are partitioned into two classes and edges connect only across classes. In a bipartite random network NPSEM, a tie between a person and a place runs both ways with the same weight, so the people's rows of the adjacency matrix determine the network. A BRNFFRCISTG is a causal model of a bipartite random network NPSEM that satisfies the conditions of an RNFFRCISTG, except that single-world independence takes each person's network weights, their row of the adjacency matrix, rather than each graph generator, as a single variable (@def-brnffrcistg). That row belongs to the person's observational unit (@def-bipartite-npsem-ie), so no contagion, identical structural distributions and single-world independence apply to it like any other covariate.
